recentItems.title: Did the West IGNORE Putin’s aggression for too long?
recentItems.description:
What influence does the UK still have on the world stage? And can it use it to prevent some of the world’s worst atrocities?

[Subscribe to our Substack newsletter: https://channel4news.substack.com/subscribe]

On this episode of the Fourcast, Krishnan Guru-Murthy is joined by the Nobel Peace Prize Laureate and member of the Standing Group on Atrocity Crimes, Oleksandra Matviichuk.

Matviichuk however says that the UK can - and should - become a ‘world leader’ in the prevention of atrocities around the world - and that doing so is in our national interest.

recentItems.title: Government says UK must prepare for emerging AI attacks
recentItems.description:
The UK government has set out its plans for regulating artificial intelligence as it warns an attack on the country is likely. 

[Subscribe to our Substack newsletter: https://channel4news.substack.com/subscribe]

AI Minister Kanishka Narayan warned about the dangers of tech giants self-policing, saying mandatory safety reporting should be introduced, along with tighter controls on the most advanced models. 

The minister’s stark warning follows the recent OpenAI breach in Australia but also that the government plans to use AI to strengthen the UK's national cyber defences.

We spoke to Nigel Inkster, who was director for operations and intelligence at MI6 and now advises on cyber-security at the International Institute for Strategic Studies. 

We began by asking whether the minister was right in saying it's likely, if not inevitable, that British systems are breached by AI.

recentItems.title: Saudi Arabia vows ‘serious response’ to deadly Houthi airport strikes
recentItems.description:
Saudi Arabia's Energy Minister has promised a “serious” response after a weekend of deadly Houthi attacks - but there are fears the escalation of the war in Yemen could draw in other players. 

[Subscribe to our Substack newsletter: https://channel4news.substack.com/subscribe]

Riyadh's King Khalid Airport will stay closed until Saturday, after it was hit by the Houthi attacks over the weekend, which killed 14 people and injured at least 320 others.

Saudi forces have responded with more air strikes on Yemen's Houthi-controlled capital Sanaa, where at least one person was killed. 

There's also been intense fighting in Taiz province, where Saudi and Yemeni government forces are battling to stop the Houthis taking the strategically-important city of Taiz.

Warning: This report contains distressing images.
